summary: Increase the default SQLite reader page-cache target from 2 MiB to 8 MiB

replay.detail: No claim replay or projection rebuild is introduced.

schema.detail: No database tables, indexes, migrations or schema version change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule or digest change; no coordinated member upgrade is required.

compatibility.detail: No client, protocol or pairing contract change. The existing SMALLCLAIMS_READ_CACHE_KIB override remains supported.

downtime.detail: No additional restart or first-open work is introduced. The process reads the cache override once; a normal daemon restart applies a changed environment setting. End-to-end restart latency was not measured.

manual.detail: Without an override, 128 retained idle readers now have about 1 GiB of nominal SQLite page-cache targets rather than 256 MiB. The writer adds 32 MiB, and the existing 512 MiB doctor reserve gives a 1568 MiB planning envelope, exceeding a 1 GiB service cap. Targets are advisory, not an RSS limit, and concurrent reader count is not capped. Memory-constrained installations can set SMALLCLAIMS_READ_CACHE_KIB=2048 in the daemon environment before restarting, or adjust their service memory limit. See docs/st3/profiling.md.

recovery.detail: No persistent state is changed. Restoring SMALLCLAIMS_READ_CACHE_KIB=2048 or swapping back the binary restores the earlier cache target on restart; no database recovery is required.
